steps.text: In a microwave safe casserole dish pour enough water to reach 1 1/2 inches in depth. Place the squash halves cut side down in the water, and pierce the skin with a fork a few times. Microwave on high for 15 to 20 minutes. Drain.
Sprinkle each half with salt and pepper to taste. Place 2 tablespoons butter and 2 tablespoons brown sugar in each half.
Broil 5 minutes, or until butter is melted. Mix the melted butter and sugar into the flesh, and serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Nana's Acorn Squash
raw_recipe.description: Acorn squash is microwaved until tender, and then broiled with butter and brown sugar.

review.reviewBody: Simple, quick and delicious! I love acorn squash and my Mom always used to make it this way. I'm so glad I found this recipe. This is a fall and winter classic and what's great is it takes virtually no time at all! If you want to spice things up add a little cinnamon or nutmeg.

This microwave method for squash is really great. This is exactly the way I've made acorn squash many times. I like to add some cinnamon to the brown sugar too. I don't usually bother with the broiling-- I just put back into the microwave to melt the butter. I have discovered that you can also cook a squash in the microwave without cutting it. Just wash and pierce the skin of the squash and put it right into the microwave. Carefully cut the squash in half and the seeds are easily scraped out. I usually do this when the squash is kind of small. If it's a large one, it concerns me that the squash won't cook all the way evenly.

I cannot cut an acorn squash without piercing the outside and microwaving it for 2-4 minutes, depending on size. Other than that, I made this as written. It was just as good as baking it in the oven. Actually, I liked it better! One suggestion I'll make is to use a deep dish to make it in the microwave. I only did one half of the squash and used a pyrex square dish with about a 3" height. Most of the water boiled over. Fortunately, I placed two very absorbent paper towels under the dish, which made cleanup easier. Since I had microwaved the squash to soften in order to cut it in half, I only cooked my large squash for 15 minutes. I love acorn squash and have always had it made with butter, brown sugar and cinnamon. This recipe is a keeper!

Delicious! I love acorn squash and this was fantastic! I did cut back the butter and brown sugar, though. I feel the full amount would have been too sweet. Also drizzled a bit of maple syrup over the top, then broiled quickly to crisp things up.
Easy to make and so delicious! As per another poster, I added a splash of bourbon and used maple syrup instead of brown sugar. Yummy. It's a keeper.
I used maple syrup instead of brown sugar & topped it with roasted pecans. So delicious!

Love Acorn squaw!!! This makes the whole thing EASY...but I do something a little different- into each half (after turning over) I add a small container of cinnamon applesauce with a little brown sugar added and dot each with small pieces of butter. YUM- my man LOVES it and saves his for dessert!!!! You can add a drizzle of maple syrup into squash before the applesauce for extra flavor.

Honestly, this was the first time I had ever made acorn squash but it won't be the last. I cooked the whole squash 8 min in the microwave then cut it in half, scooped out the guts and added the butter and brown sugar - I also sprinkled in a bit so cayenne pepper for a little kick. A few minutes under the broiler and it was crunchy perfection!

Never had an acorn squash that I can remember, a friend gave me one and I found this recipe which was simple, quick and absolutely delicious. I just added a little cinnamon. Next time, I want to add some chopped pecans to swim in that pool of goodness…I read another recipe somewhere that had them and I think it would be a great addition.
Quick and easy, broiling in toaster oven frees up oven for main course. Loved maple syrup and butter, will try brown sugar and butter next time.
Great way to fix acorn squash. Way too much butter! add a teaspoon of butter, Tsp. Of brown sugar and cinnamon for that super Fall favor
Great recipe! I've made similar, but always in the oven. This way is far easier and tastes fantastic. Thanks for sharing!

My mother, her mother and her grandmother all made this exact recipe only putting the butter and brown sugar into the raw salted squash then baking, cut side up at 375 F until done (time will vary with size of squash). Bonus is only 1 pan to clean
This was delicious and easy! I used half the butter and brown sugar, andded some cinnamon and nutmeg ant it was just right for us.
Grew up baking in the oven. Love the fast and easy of microwave recipe
It was an easy but a VERY tasty recipe. My husband had never eaten acorn squash in his 65+ years and he really liked it, so I will be making it again.

This is a great squash recipe! Super easy!! To make cutting the uncooked squash easier, poke the squash with a sharp knife a few times, then microwave for 3-4 minutes whole. Then allow to cool enough to handle, then cut in half and proceed with the recipe.
Use half the butter

This is the way to do it. I've always baked the cut squash in the oven for over an hour, and even then you can't be sure the squash is soft all the way through. Microwaving first to steam it until thoroughly tender is a great idea -- it saves all that oven energy, and it's so much faster. Thanks for sharing this!
I made it as is except I just put it back in the microwave to melt butter and then use a fork to mix it all together,
